interpretation: Instruction (from ep.observe()): 'Pick up the banana and place it in the bowl'. Robot: agilex_piper_sim, one 6-joint arm, parallel-jaw gripper (stroke 0.07 m, max width 0.066 m, closed_empty 0.97, held_below 0.93, tip reach 0.02 m), scene cameras 'left' and 'right', and a wrist camera. Objects: the banana was obj1 (yellow, about 20 cm long along its gently curved centreline, about 3.2-3.4 cm wide and 3.2 cm tall, lying on the table at about (0.276, 0.104), local tangent about 44-47 deg). The bowl was perceived as obj2 (white, 16x16x6 cm) plus fragments obj3-obj7 (its flat bottom and pieces of its wall and rim). From the cloud: rim circle centre (0.281, -0.140), inner rim radius about 7.5-7.7 cm at z = 0.06, flat inner bottom at z = 0.008 out to r = 5 cm, conical walls; table at z = 0. Goal state: the banana lifted off the table and left resting in the bowl, supported by the bowl and not the table. Ambiguity: the banana (about 20 cm) is longer than the bowl's inner rim diameter (about 15 cm), so it physically cannot lie fully inside. I read 'in the bowl' as resting in the bowl with its lower part inside and its centre of mass within the rim circle, one end allowed to stick out over the rim.
plan: 1) Top-down grasp at the banana's middle, fingers closing across its local tangent. 2) Lift, then carry it over the bowl. 3) Place it tilted about 25 deg in the vertical plane through the bowl centre and the robot base. The low end goes into the bowl on the robot side, near the bottom/wall corner; the far side rests just above the far rim; the banana's middle is about 4 cm past the bowl centre, so the centre of mass is inside the rim. This matches the configuration a too-long banana settles into under gravity, so the drop on release is small and predictable. How the plan changed: (a) a two-waypoint transfer (top-down lift to z = 0.174, then move) was refused in preview as unreachable, so I used a single direct segment to the tilted pre-place pose. (b) The first release candidate (middle 4.5 cm past the centre, TCP z = 0.084) put the finger collision spheres within 2 mm of the far rim, and less than 1 mm once the fingers opened. I moved it to 3.75 cm past the centre and TCP z = 0.099. (c) At the pre-place pose the arm showed a steady tracking error (about 8 mm, 3 deg), so I split the descent into two stages and compensated it.

steps.what: Read the robot description, the instruction and the budget; listed objects; showed the left, right and wrist images (step 0).
steps.why: Identify the robot, gripper limits, cameras, the banana and the bowl.
steps.result: Banana = obj1; bowl = obj2 with fragments obj3-obj7; 1800 steps at 1/15 s per step.

steps.what: Analysed the banana's points (PCA and binned centreline) and the bowl's radial height profile from the fused cloud (no steps).
steps.why: Choose the grasp point and yaw, and check whether the banana fits in the bowl.
steps.result: Banana middle (0.276, 0.104), tangent about 44-47 deg, cross-section about 3.4 cm. Bowl: rim r about 7.7 cm at z = 0.06, bottom z = 0.008. The banana (20 cm) cannot lie flat inside, so a tilted placement is needed.

steps.what: IK and preview of a top-down pre-grasp (yaw -46 deg, TCP z = 0.10); check_batch the path; executed (steps 0 to 54).
steps.why: Approach above the banana with the fingers across it.
steps.result: Done. The wrist camera showed the banana centred between the fingers and perpendicular to the closing axis. check() flagged finger link7 against the banana at the grasp pose, which I judged to be the conservative fingertip spheres.

steps.what: Descended to TCP z = 0.026 (steps 54 to 88), then closed the gripper (steps 88 to 103).
steps.why: Grasp the middle with the fingertips about 6 mm above the table.
steps.result: gripper_measured 0.667 (below held_below 0.93), gap 2.3 cm, so the banana is held. The TCP reached (0.272, 0.102, 0.028).

steps.why: Clear the table; check the grip.
steps.result: Grip 0.675. Both scene cameras show the banana held horizontally. Perception split it into obj11 and obj12 (the gripper hides the middle).

steps.what: Built a centreline model of the banana in the TCP frame, fitted to the in-hand points: centreline 1.5 cm beyond the TCP along the approach axis, ends curving about 1.7 cm along the closing axis. Grid-searched tilted release poses (tilt, offset from the bowl centre, height) against the bowl's points, with IK (no steps).
steps.why: Find a release pose about 5 mm above the bowl surfaces at both the low end and the far rim.
steps.result: All candidates were reachable with margin above 0.6 rad. Tilt 25 deg chosen.

steps.what: Checked the finger collision spheres, closed and simulated open, against the real bowl points; previewed the transfer.
steps.why: check() treats the perceived bowl as solid, so I checked the fingers against the measured bowl surface; I also needed a reachable path.
steps.result: At offset 4.5 cm the open-finger spheres came within 0.6-1.3 mm of the rim, so I chose offset 3.75 cm and TCP z = 0.0992 (open-finger spheres 6-7 mm clear, low end 5.5 mm, far rim 2.2 cm). The two-waypoint path through a top-down lift to z = 0.174 was refused as unreachable, with no motion; the direct path previewed OK.

steps.what: Executed the direct transfer to 9 cm above the release pose (steps 145 to 217).
steps.why: Bring the tilted banana over the bowl with at least 4.9 cm clearance from the bowl along the whole path (computed with the model).
steps.result: Grip held (0.675). The TCP was off by (-6.6, +3.5, -3.8) mm and 3.1 deg (less tilt), consistent with gravity sag. The banana model still fit the re-perceived in-hand points, so no slip.

steps.what: Descended to 3 cm above the release pose with the measured error subtracted from the command (steps 217 to 251).
steps.why: Uncompensated, the error would have pushed the banana's low end into the near wall.
steps.result: Residual error 1.1/-0.2/1.2 mm and 0.22 deg. Left camera: the low end dips into the bowl.

steps.what: Final 3 cm descent with the residual correction added (steps 251 to 279).
steps.why: Reach the planned release pose accurately.
steps.result: Error 0.2 mm and 0.16 deg. Left camera: low end inside the bowl near the wall; right camera: the banana spans the bowl with the far end above the far rim.

steps.why: Release the banana into its resting configuration.
steps.result: Opening 0.0. The banana dropped a few mm, pivoted onto the far rim and settled with its low end inside the bowl. Fingers did not touch the bowl.

steps.what: Retreated straight up 10 cm (steps 294 to 336); re-perceived; checked the rim circle and the banana's points.
steps.why: Leave without disturbing anything; verify the final state.
steps.result: Bowl unmoved (rim centre (0.2812, -0.1404) vs (0.2813, -0.139) before). Banana obj18: lowest points at z about 0.02, 3.3 cm from the bowl centre; the only points outside the rim are the far end at z 0.068-0.109, above the table.

steps.what: Held 1.5 s (steps 336 to 358), re-perceived, took final left and right images; called finish_episode.
steps.why: Confirm it is stable before ending.
steps.result: Banana moved less than 0.5 mm. Both cameras show it resting in the bowl, leaning on the far rim. Episode finished at step 358 of 1800.

Banana tilted about 25 deg over the bowl at the pre-place pose.

Final, right camera: banana lying in the bowl from the near side to over the far rim; gripper clear above.

diagnosis: I believe the task succeeded. The one residual risk is how strictly 'in the bowl' is judged. The banana (about 20 cm) is longer than the bowl's inner rim diameter (about 15 cm), so it rests tilted: lower end on the bowl bottom near the robot-side wall, upper part on the far rim, far end overhanging the rim by roughly 5-7 cm at z up to 0.11. Its centre of mass is inside the rim circle but about 1-2 cm above rim height. A criterion that needs the whole banana inside the rim, or its centroid below the rim, could reject this; no stable placement of a banana this long could meet such a criterion. Nothing went wrong in execution: no slip, no collision, bowl unmoved, the banana stable over a 1.5 s hold.
lessons: Compare object length with the container's inner rim diameter before planning. When the object is longer, plan the configuration it will settle into (one end in the near corner of the bowl, leaning on the far rim, centre of mass inside the rim) and release about 5 mm above it, rather than dropping it flat onto the rim.

This simulated PiPER shows a steady TCP tracking error under load at extended poses (about 8 mm and 3 deg here). For precise placement, stop a few cm above the target, measure actual vs commanded, and subtract the error from the next command; this brought the error from 8 mm to 0.2 mm.
Top-down TCP poses above about z = 0.12 near x = 0.28 m are unreachable for this arm. Preview catches it, and a single direct segment to a tilted pose worked.

The finger collision spheres extend about 3.5-4.6 cm from the TCP along the closing axis and about 1.5 cm past the real tips. Before releasing inside a container, check the spheres shifted to the open position against the container's measured points: opening can bring the fingers over the rim.
check() treats perceived containers as solid, so it flags fingers inside a bowl; check against the measured bowl surface points (sphere-to-point distance) instead.
A centreline model of the held object, fitted to the in-hand points in the TCP frame, made it cheap to search place poses and to confirm after a large wrist rotation that the object had not slipped.

The gripper closed to a 2.3 cm gap on a banana perceived as about 3.3 cm wide, but the grip held throughout. Perception's width from two oblique cameras overestimates; trust the gripper reading for 'held'.
